sentences.text: Antarctosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous.
Describing Antarctosaurus is problematic because no species is known from complete remains and the association of bones is questionable.
Antarctosaurus was a genus of four species of sauropod dinosaur belonging to the titanosaur group.
The genus Antarctosaurus was established by Friedrich von Huene in 1929.
Phylogenetic analyses place Antarctosaurus as a sister taxon to Vahiny and Jainosaurus, close to the clade Lognkosauria.
Researchers usually regard the skull and skeleton of A. wichmannianus as titanosaurian, though they may not belong to the same individual.
The type species of Antarctosaurus measured up to 18 meters in length and weighed around 34 tons.
A. wichmannianus has been considered a Lithostrotia, a group including armored titanosaurs, although no shield was associated with the remains.
The type species was placed as a possible nemegtosaurine.
The total estimated length of Antarctosaurus wichmannianus is around 17 meters.
The femurs of Antarctosaurus giganteus measure 2.35 meters in length, among the largest of any known sauropod.
A 1956 reconstruction by Carlos Rusconi estimated the length of A. giganteus at around 30 meters.
Based on some estimates, A. giganteus is considered among the heaviest known land animals.
A 2016 study estimated the weight of A. giganteus at 39.5 metric tons based on limb bone circumference.
In 2020, Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated the length of A. giganteus at 30.5 meters and its weight at 45 metric tons.
A. giganteus may have been one of the largest dinosaurs discovered, estimated to reach 23 to 30 meters in length and weigh 69 tons.
The genus Antarctosaurus was described by Friedrich von Huene in 1929.
The type species A. wichmannianus and the second species A. giganteus were both described by Friedrich von Huene in 1929.
Remains of Antarctosaurus were first mentioned in print in 1916 but were not fully described until 1929.
The fossil remains of Antarctosaurus wichmannianus were assigned the specimen number MACN 6904.
The known fossils of A. wichmannianus include skull fragments, a neck vertebra, a tail vertebra, ribs, and limb bones, including a femur 1.39 meters tall.
The type specimen of A. giganteus (MLP 26-316) includes femurs, pubis bones, a damaged tibia, ribs, tail vertebrae fragments, and six unidentifiable bones.
Antarctosaurus jaxarticus is known only from a single femur that resembles one attributed to Jainosaurus.
The most notable known remains are two femurs measuring 2.35 meters in length, among the largest known for any dinosaur.
Antarctosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 78 million years ago, in what is now South America and possibly Asia.
Researchers suggest the squared-off jaws of A. wichmannianus indicate specialized feeding habits, possibly involving low vegetation or floating plants.
It is debated whether the square jaw shape is a convergence with rebbachisaurids or truly belongs to Antarctosaurus, as the recent discovery of Bonitasaura suggests the latter.
Despite their large size, the femurs of A. giganteus are somewhat gracile in construction.
Antarctosaurus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous Period.
Fossils of A. wichmannianus come from the Anacleto Formation in Argentina, which is probably early Campanian in age.
Antarctosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Researchers are uncertain whether the remains attributed to the type species A. wichmannianus belong to the same individual or even the same genus.
Some researchers regard A. giganteus as a nomen dubium due to the scarcity of remains.
It is debated whether the square lower jaw of A. wichmannianus belongs to the species or to a rebbachisaurid sauropod similar to Nigersaurus.
